newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mitsubishi Australia sees A$450 mln new investment.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Australia sees A$450 mln new investment.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd, one of the country's four car makers, said on Friday that it was confident about investing up to A$450 million in a new model following the national government's backdown on tariff reductions.
"Our next investment needs to be decided by the end of 1998," managing director Mike Quinn told reporters. "It will a number of somewhere between A$400 million and A$450 million."
"I think after last night's decision (by the Howard government) you can look very positively towards the next investment," he said.
Mitsubishi expects to produce between 65,000 and 70,000 of its Magna car range this calendar year, with exports of up to 25,000.
Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday evening that car import tariffs would be frozen at 15 percent from the year 2000 and would be cut to 10 percent in January 2005.
He rejected more dramatic cuts urged by his chief industry advisory group, the Productivity Commission, which wanted only a five percent rate by the year 2004.
Car makers quickly welcomed the plan -- which will be reviewed again in 2005 -- as a sensible measure creating stability for their future investment and saving jobs.
Mitsubishi and three other companies -- Ford Motor Co, General Motors Corp and Toyota Motor Corp -- have manufacturing plants in Australia.
